title: An ending asks for proportionate consequences

captions.physics: Ending an earlier form of action

meaning: Shared closure of an earlier form through recognising its completion is emotionally answered by sensitivity to proportionate consequences.
text: In this Energy Field, Death occupies two different positions. In the physical position, it describes shared actions that end an earlier form or phase; in energy, it motivates recognising completion rather than automatically continuing the former approach. Justice in emotions adds sensitivity to proportionate consequences. The overall tone can therefore be organised: you carry out a particular ending and want to stop retaining an outgrown form, while emotionally noticing how its final costs and results are distributed between you.

For example, you permanently close a shared project for exchanging belongings. Recognising that the former format no longer continues, you return remaining items and complete agreements. Relief appears when the last tasks are distributed according to actual capacities. **We are ending this activity and want its consequences to fit each person’s participation.** The feeling of fairness concerns a particular closure; it does not turn the whole history into a competition over merit. The practical ending and its emotional assessment remain distinct.

A difficulty arises if determination to finish becomes a reason to overlook the other person’s inconvenience. Proportion is replaced by speed: what matters is putting an end to things quickly. Alternatively, endless accounting postpones the final actions. Death’s two roles intensify no prediction of loss, and Justice in emotions supplies no final verdict. Closure can be real while its consequences and emotional experience still require clarification from both people.
